 ::JUDGMENT:

: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 SCCH-5 for the relief of compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 13.02.2023 at about 4.30 p.m. petitioner was crossing the road near Vishal Mart, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru at that time, a driver of the Passenger Auto Rickshwaw (Three Wheeler) bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL-5779 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, due to the accident she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Kava Sri Sai Hospital,
wherein she took treatment as inpatient and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 50 years, hale and healthy, working as employee in SCCH-5 private firm, thereby earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.

Due to the accidental injuries,
she could not attend to her work, undergone lot of mental agony, pain and suffering and lost her income.
With regard to accident in crime No.70/2023 is registered against the driver of the said autorickshaw before the Rajajinagar Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared before court hence placed exparte.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and submitted that, it has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of SCCH-5 autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AL-5779 and liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, it seeks protection available under Sec.147 and Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.159 of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that driver of the said auto was not holding valid and effective driving Varalakshmi.N vs Nataraj.D on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92590072/
2 licence at the time of accident and offending vehicle did not had valid permit and fitness certificate to ply on the road.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 13.02.2023 at about 4.30 p.m. near SCCH-5 Vishal Mart, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of one Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL- 5779 dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, husband/next friend and natural guardian of the petitioner is examined as PW-1, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Manipal Hospital is examined as PW-2,
Medical Record incharge at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital is examined as PW-3 and marked 22 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22.

On the other hand, RTO, Shanthinagar is examined as RW-1 Legal Manager of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-2 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
SCCH-5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :
As per final order for the  following:

: : REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove the case, husband/next friend and natural guardian of the petitioner is examined as PW-1, in his chief-examination PW-1 has reiterated the facts narrated in the petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked medical certificate issued by Dr.Shivaraj K.K. as Ex.P.1, copy of FIR as Ex.P.2, copy of complaint as Ex.P.3, copy SCCH-5 of spot mahazar with sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice with reply as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet with statement of witnesses as Ex.P.8.

Varalakshmi.N vs Nataraj.D on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92590072/
3 9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon and Medical Record Incharge as PW-2 and PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 13.02.2023 as alleged in the petition.
10. Per contra, RTO, Shanthinagar is examined as RW-1 and marked copy of details of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL-5779 as Ex.R.1.
R.W.1 stated that as on 30.10.2022 the vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05-AL- 5779 was registered as per documents.
R.W.1 specifically SCCH-5 stated that the auto was not having permit to ply prior to 01.08.2023.
Nothing elicited during the cross examination of R.W.1 to rebut that as on on the date of accident the offending Auto was holding valid permit to ply nor produced any permit copy by the petitioner.

11. Further examined Legal Manager of respondent No.1 as RW-2 and marked as authorization letter Ex.R.2 and copy of policy along with terms and conditions as Ex.R.3. R.W.2 deposed that as on the date of accident the driver of auto was not holding valid DL,Permit and fitness certificate to ply the auto.
During the cross examination of R.W.2 nothing is elicited to discard this contention.
12. The respondent No.2 not disputed the occurrence of accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.

In the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal SCCH-5 held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 13.02.2023 at about 4.30 p.m. when she was crossing the road near Vishal Mart, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru.
13. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Passenger Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL- 5779.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, PW-1 has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the PW-1, petitioner had sustained TBI with left FTP hgemorrhagic Contusion, Multiple Soft Tissue injuries, Sepsis with aspiration pneumonia, newly detected DMT2 and other injury all over the body.

In this regard he has furnished SCCH-5 medical certificate issued by Dr.Shivaraj K.K. as Ex.P.1, copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, wherein petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 13.02.2023 to 05.03.2023.

Further PW-1 produced medical bills of Rs.77,192/- marked as Ex.P.11 and medical prescriptions as Ex.P.12.
15.

Further Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon, Manipal Hospital is examined as PW-2 and marked clinical notes as Ex.P.13, authorization letter as Ex.P.14, assessment report as Ex.P.15, MRI Report as Ex.P.16 and MRI Films as Ex.P.17. PW-2
has assessed permanent neurological disability of 40%.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 13% of SCCH-5 neurological disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

16. As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 50 years, for proof of her age, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.10, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the Varalakshmi.N vs Nataraj.D on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92590072/
4 petitioner as 01.01.1973 and the alleged accident is occurred on 13.02.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.10 age of the petitioner is considered about 50 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 17. As per petitioner's case, she was working as employee in private firm, thereby earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no SCCH-5 documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.16,000/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9, petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital for a period of 20 days.

As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined SCCH-5 petitioner on 08.12.2023 i.e., nearly after 10 months and on examination date as per version of PW-2 and by considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least 6months to recover.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.16,000/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.96,000/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
19. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.77,692/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for SCCH-5 this treatment is concerned.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that,
petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 13.02.2023.
So as per Ex.P.7 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained abrasion over right elbow, fracture of right temporal bone, left temporal lobe contusion, cerebral odema, which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Nataraj D. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
20.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
SCCH-5 Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 3,24,480-00 Varalakshmi.N vs Nataraj.D on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92590072/
5 2. Pain
and sufferings 25,000-00
3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 77,692-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 96,000-00 period Total 5,53,172-00 21.

Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,53,172/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.01637189670000 which is valid for the period from 07.10.2022 to 06.10.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 13.02.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of SCCH-5 accident, insurance policy was in force but the respondent No.1 violated the terms and conditions of policy.

As per the cross examination version of R.W.1 from 03.01.2023 the permit was valid for Auto bearing Registration No.KA-05-AD-1815 and same was replaced to auto bearing registration No.KA-05-AL-5779 on 01.03.2023.
The accident occurred on 13.02.2023,thus it is clear that as on the date of accident there is no permit to offending auto to ply.

Admittedly insurance of offending auto is valid from 07.10.2022 to 06.10.2023 hence the liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order and recover the same from Respondent No.1 with due SCCH-5 process of law.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,53,172/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Fifty Three Thousand One Hundred Seventy Two Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover the same from respondent No.1 with due process of law.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
